title: Per-tenant priority SLO tiers, adaptive burn-rate throttles, and staged fallback policies for Dedicated customers
creator: Asha Menon
description: PRD-level ticket to define per-tenant SLO tiers for Dedicated customers, an adaptive burn-rate based throttling policy, and staged fallback/rollout gates. Goal: provide clear latency & availability contracts for paying tenants, automated protective behavior when error budgets deplete, and deterministic rollout gates for canaries and progressive releases. This ticket covers targets, measurement windows, incident/rollback triggers, expected operator runbooks, and the observable signals required to gate rollouts and automated fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Define at least three per-tenant SLO tiers (Gold/Silver/Bronze) with explicit latency P50/P95/P99 envelopes for the most common request classes (chat/streaming, single-shot generation, embeddings).
Specify availability SLOs (monthly uptime %) and daily error budget computation method for each tier.
Document adaptive burn-rate policy: how burn rate is computed, thresholds for automated throttling, and graduated throttling steps (10/30/50% of new requests).

Design staged fallback behaviors: model-variant fallback (quantized/lighter model), regional failover, and degrade-to-embeddings-only for read-only routes. Each fallback must include targeted latency and quality impact statements.
Define rollout gates for canaries: metric set, minimum measurement window, threshold pass/fail rules, and required sample size per tenant.
Provide dashboard mocks and alert definitions (SI thresholds, burn-rate alerts, SLO burn > 25% within 4h) and link to dashboards in Console.
Provide an automated test harness for canary validation that simulates tenant traffic patterns and verifies gate behavior locally and in staging.
Operational runbook: clear steps to manually engage/disengage throttles, roll back fallback policies, and communicate incidents to affected tenants.
decisions: Use per-tenant rolling 30d window for availability SLO calculations; use 1d rolling window for short-term burn-rate detection.
Classify traffic into three workload classes for SLOs: interactive-streaming, interactive-batched, offline-embeddings.
Adaptive throttling will be implemented in the request-routing tier with tokens per tenant and ability to apply percentage-based shedding policies.
Fallback sequence prioritized as: (1) model-variant fallback on same region, (2) regional failover to secondary region, (3) apply degraded routing (e.g., disable streaming) for affected tenant.
open_questions: What constitutes an acceptable fidelity drop when falling back to a quantized model for Gold tenants? (engineering to propose delta metrics)
Should burn-rate-based throttling be tenant-visible (via header/error code) or entirely opaque?
How do contractual SLAs adjust billing/credits when automated throttles or fallbacks are applied? Finance/legal needs to weigh in.
notes: Reference: existing operational playbook PM-75812 (runbooks) and PM-2891 (hosted SLOs) for measurement primitives.
Prototype dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/proto-dedicated-slos (mock link for design review).
Suggested experiment schedule: 1) lab sim, 2) small-dedicated canary (5 tenants), 3) multi-tenant pilot (20 tenants), 4) full rollout.
